history.method: Normalized identifiers and titles by casefolding, NFKD and alphanumeric projection, including prior tar/gzip members; also checked the early source index.

OpenSwarm synchronized USV hydrophone SmartMesh → Zenodo experiment archives and published ROS interface definitions.
evidence: Both full publisher-checksummed experimental ZIP files. Read all 10 CSV telemetry members, headers of all 10 WAV companions, and recoverable complete message records in the 8 named MCAP members. Three stationary sensing buoys and a mobile four-metre engine-noise source vessel, across two dates. External video archives were not needed for the clock/coverage comparison.
endpoint_definitions: Group by trial and physical usv folder/filename. Treat string utc_time values as shared numeric SmartMesh labels where present and unique within a vehicle. The source specifies nominal 2 Hz service; direct counts here require identical recorded labels and do not assume these integers are Unix epoch times. Request neither interpolation nor nearest-neighbour association. MCAP log/publish nanoseconds and the string timestamp within StreamData are kept separate; GPSRAW.fix_type 6 is the source-defined RTK-fixed code.
counts: 14,295 CSV rows, including 46 with missing utc_time. On April usv3, 130 rows have repeated numeric labels within that vehicle. Across available complete MCAP records, 12,873 RMS messages and 18,375 GPS messages were decoded. All 12,873 RMS messages match a CSV row by payload timestamp, node ID, UTC label and nav status. This check concerns these four metadata fields. The three incomplete April MCAPs are counted through complete chunks; the April usv4 MCAP member is zero bytes. Its two separate CSV logs each contain one row. March has four complete bags.
integrity: ZIP archive hashes match the publisher for both dates, so the following observations concern the archived members. April usv1 and usv3 stop within top-level chunk records; April usv2 stops within a message index. April usv1 CSV has a trailing 861-byte null-only line, which is excluded. WAV frame counts are header declarations, not verification of every sound sample.
time_comparison: USV1 and USV2 both use embedded node_id=1. They share 1,740 unique labels in March and 3,418 in April. Median local payload timestamp of USV2 minus USV1 at that label is +1,499.717324 ms and +13.388851 ms respectively. At none of those matches are local timestamps exactly equal. Receiver/host timestamp discrepancy includes logger and system offsets; the labels do not identify a packet sent by one boat to the other. Cross-node hardware sampling skew and command-to-motion latency remain unobserved.
reproduction: Fetch both experiment ZIPs. Run python derive_openswarm.py DATA OUT with Python 3.11+, mcap, NumPy and pandas. Reads fixed hashes before parsing; outputs 8 trial/vehicle rows, 10 file rows and 12 within-trial vehicle-pair comparisons. Physical identity is preserved even when mote IDs repeat.
